text:
**LinkedIn Post:**

---

🥖 Mistral just dropped "Le Chonk," and the most interesting part isn't the size.

Mistral Large 4 is now on Hugging Face: a ~1T-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with roughly 50B active parameters, a 1M-token context window, and native image + text input.

The cybersecurity results are what caught my attention.

🔐 **82% on vulnerability reproduction and patching** in the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index. That's the highest reported score on that test. The model has to reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then fix it. According to Mistral, several closed frontier models score near zero on this test because they refuse to attempt it.

This matters for defenders. You usually can't patch a vulnerability without first reproducing it. Incident response and vuln research often look like attacks to a content filter. And if your security tooling depends on someone else's API, you can lose access in the middle of an incident.

Open weights put the deployment and the usage policy in your hands. The model still has guardrails: its average refusal rate on harmful cyber prompts (JailbreakBench, StrongREJECT, AgentHarm) is higher than any other open-weight model's.

📊 **Other highlights:**
• 93% on Cybench (40 security competition challenges)
• 93.3% attack resistance on Lakera's B3 prompt-injection benchmark
• 61.7% on DeepSWE v1.1, and a Coding Agent Index score ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro and Qwen3.8 Max
• #5 open-weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index

🧠 **Under the hood:** it uses two kinds of sparsity at once. A router picks 4 of 128 experts (plus 1 shared expert) for each token. A DeepSeek-style sparse attention indexer picks which earlier positions each token attends to. A 1.6B Pixtral encoder handles vision.

🛠️ **Day-0 ecosystem support:** Transformers, vLLM (NVFP4 on Blackwell, with a built-in speculative-decoding drafter), llama.cpp GGUFs, TRL fine-tuning, HF Inference Endpoints, and Dell Enterprise Hub. The 2-bit quant even runs on a single 512GB Mac Studio M3 Ultra, at about 15 tok/s.

For builders, the opportunity is to distill smaller security models from its traces or run RL on reproduce-then-patch tasks, since those come with a verifiable reward. Teams can build cyber tooling around their own codebase, crash logs, and malware samples without sending anything to a third party.

Note that it ships under the Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License, an MIT derivative with limits on model-as-a-service offerings. Check the terms before you build a product on it.

What would you build with a capable, open-weight security model? 👇

#AI #OpenSource #Cybersecurity #LLM #MistralAI #HuggingFace #MachineLearning

---

**Before posting, check one inconsistency:** the article says 49B active parameters, but the model ID is `Mistral-Large-4-1T-A52B`, which suggests 52B. I wrote "roughly 50B" to stay safe, but it's worth confirming on the model card.
